_readme: JUDGMENT, not computed. Every one of the 18 (item, language) pairs flagged by src/mgsm_translation_number_audit.py after its two automated fixes (Spanish comma-decimal parsing; Japanese single-digit counter-word suppression) was read by hand against the English source. This file records that reading. The audit script's flags are a first-pass heuristic; this file is the human-facing verdict. Anne should spot-check these, especially the two marked real_defect.

mgsm_trilingual_057.note: The Japanese premise states the delivery truck is 'already loaded with 33 identical boxes' (小さな箱を33個積んでおり), a specific quantity absent from English entirely, while the question still asks for the maximum number of boxes that CAN be loaded -- an internal contradiction not present in the English original. This is the more serious of the two confirmed defects: it doesn't just drop information, it inserts a false premise.

mgsm_trilingual_139.note: Japanese omits '22 more than' entirely, rendering the relation as pink = 4*blue instead of pink = 4*blue + 22. Changes the required formula, not just the phrasing. Already identified in the Week 4 audit; reconfirmed here by the systematic pass.

mgsm_trilingual_028.note: '1か所目と2か所目' (the 1st place, the 2nd place) renders English's ordinal words 'first'/'second' with digit+counter.

mgsm_trilingual_039.note: '6時間' = 'six hours' (digit-for-word); '3分の1' / '3分の2' = Japanese fraction notation (X-bun-no-Y = Y/X) for English's word-form 'one-third' / 'two-thirds'. Same quantities, different notation.

mgsm_trilingual_129.note: '1時間$150' = '$150 an hour' -- Japanese writes the implicit 'an/per' as explicit '1'.

mgsm_trilingual_178.note: '10匹多く' = 'ten more' (digit-for-word; a 2-digit exception to the usual single-digit cardinal pattern, verified by hand rather than by the automated filter).

mgsm_trilingual_179.note: '1時間に10ドル' = '$10 an hour' (implicit 'an' -> explicit '1'); '最初の2週間' = 'the first two weeks' (digit-for-word 'two').

mgsm_trilingual_183.note: '1600メートルリレー' names the relay by its total distance (a real naming convention for this race in Japanese), while still separately stating '4名が...400メートルずつ' (4 members x 400m each) -- no information is lost, the total is just also stated up front.

mgsm_trilingual_233.note: '3分の1' = 'one-third' (Japanese fraction notation), appearing twice in the source for EN's two 'one-third' phrases.

mgsm_trilingual_246.note: '1週間に4回' = '4 times a week' (implicit 'a' -> explicit '1').

mgsm_trilingual_087.note: 'あと3年' = 'three more years' (digit-for-word); '12月' = 'December' -- Japanese numbers months (1月-12月) instead of naming them, a structural calendar-convention difference, not a content change.

mgsm_trilingual_062.note: Spanish writes '$50 000' with a SPACE as the thousands separator, a convention this audit's regex doesn't parse (it expects period-as-thousands, comma-as-decimal). Same value, 50000, as English's '$50,000'. Not fixed in the script to avoid over-matching ordinary spaces between separate numbers; documented here instead.

mgsm_trilingual_195.note: The same Spanish sentence mixes both decimal conventions: '$1,20' (comma decimal, correct Spanish convention) and '$0.30' (period decimal, English convention, left unconverted). Same value, 0.30, either way -- an internal formatting inconsistency in the official dataset, not a content error.
